content.text: {"answer":"To improve LLM self-training by choosing varied ways to solve a problem (not only correct ones), the most directly aligned paper is “Strategically Diverse Sampling for Self-Training.” It argues that self-training data is often built by sampling i.i.d. responses and filtering mainly for correctness, overrepresenting strategies a model already prefers, and proposes “strategically diverse” data that varies the substantive approach to the problem. It introduces GROOT (sampling distinct paths from a hierarchical tree of approaches) and Verbalized Sampling (producing an unstructured set of approaches), and reports improved performance on difficult tasks versus IID-trained counterparts, including cases where training on strategically diverse but incorrect traces can outperform IID distillation from a much larger teacher. [1]\n\nRelated work measures and mitigates diversity collapse: “Measuring and Mitigating Solution Mode Collapse in RLVR” finds that RL with verifiable rewards concentrates probability onto fewer correct solution modes, and proposes Re:Max to store one verified example per discovered mode and train uniformly on those stored modes. [2] “Reasoning Path Divergence” instead focuses on a “one problem, multiple solutions” paradigm, using Reasoning Path Divergence to curate maximally diverse reasoning trajectories and fine-tune a model for higher output diversity and pass@k. [3] Finally, “Vocabulary Dropout” targets diversity in co-evolutionary self-play curricula by masking proposer logits to prevent collapse toward a narrow problem distribution. [6]","grounded":true}
